blocker1ConcurrencySnapshotProvenance.problem: After awaiting a mutation, submit() wrote directly into legalSnapshotRef/generalSnapshotRef, React state (setMapsUrl/setWhatsapp), success counters, and the final outcome presentation WITHOUT proving the restaurant context was still the same, that the submitted value was still the latest UI value, or that the user had not edited that field again while the RPC was in flight. Two concrete examples named by the audit: (A) restaurant switch A->B while save(A) is in flight -- a late successful A mutation could overwrite B's snapshot; (B) Maps URL -- user submits X, types Y while in flight, late success wrote snapshot=X AND called setMapsUrl(X), erasing Y from the UI.
blocker1ConcurrencySnapshotProvenance.fix: submit() now captures a save-attempt identity token via lib/restaurant-context-guard.ts's EXISTING useRestaurantContextGuard() hook (guard.beginRequest(restaurantId)) -- REUSED, not reinvented, per the mandate's own 'keep this narrow' instruction and the same mechanism load() already uses. Immediately after EVERY await in submit() (both the success path and the catch block), `if (!token.isCurrent()) return;` aborts the ENTIRE remaining continuation for a stale save BEFORE touching any snapshot ref, any React set* call, any success counter, or the final three-way outcome presentation (setSaved/setError) -- mirroring the exact idiom already audited and in use inside load(). A restaurant switch (handleSelectRestaurant -> guard.enterContext) invalidates any in-flight token from the old restaurant in the SAME synchronous event handler, so there is no intermediate render where a stale save could still look current.
blocker1ConcurrencySnapshotProvenance.newerEditDuringSaveFix: Where submit() previously wrote a submitted value back into React state unconditionally after a successful await (setMapsUrl(currentGeneral.mapsUrl), setWhatsapp(currentGeneral.whatsapp)), the write is now a conditional updater-function form: `setX((live) => (live === rawValueCapturedAtSubmitStart ? submittedValue : live))`. It reads the TRUE current state at update time (never a stale closure) and only overwrites if the field still shows EXACTLY the value that was submitted (i.e. no new edit happened while the RPC was in flight); otherwise the newer edit is left untouched. The snapshot still advances to the submitted value, so the newer (untouched) UI value correctly remains dirty and is sent on the next Save. The legal/tax section never had this specific hazard -- it never writes a submitted value back into any setLegalXxx state, only advances legalSnapshotRef -- so only the staleness guard (not a back-write fix) was needed there.
blocker1ConcurrencySnapshotProvenance.latentDeadlockFoundAndFixed: Adding the `return`-on-stale guard introduced a NEW defect: an aborted stale continuation never reaches the `setSaving(false)` at the very end of submit(), so `saving` would stay stuck at `true` FOREVER after a restaurant switch mid-save, permanently disabling the Save button for every subsequently selected restaurant even though no save is actually in flight for it. Fixed minimally by adding `setSaving(false)` to handleSelectRestaurant, in the same synchronous reset block as resetLegalProfileState/guard.enterContext/generalSnapshotRef=null -- the new restaurant context always starts with Save available, never inheriting a stuck `saving=true` from a context that is no longer displayed. Caught by writing test C1 before this fix existed and observing the Save button for B never re-enabling; confirmed fixed once this one line was added.
blocker1ConcurrencySnapshotProvenance.defensiveFinalGuard: An additional `if (!token.isCurrent()) return;` was added immediately before the final three-way outcome block (setSaved/setError), even though it is technically already unreachable once every earlier per-await guard has returned -- the mandate explicitly lists 'presenting save outcome tied to that context' as something that must be guarded, so this is made explicit rather than relying implicitly on code order.

blocker2ContactBundleNotAtomic.problem: The 'contact group' wrapped 5 separate RPC calls (updateRestaurantPublicContact, updateRestaurantWhatsapp, updateRestaurantWhatsappEnabled, updateRestaurantSettings, setAllMerchantTrackingStatusText) in ONE try/catch. A try/catch does not make those writes atomic: if public contact succeeded and WhatsApp then failed, the group recorded zero success and the UI showed only stContactSaveError, even though public contact had already been persisted -- violating v1.1's own promise of unambiguous partial-save reporting, but INSIDE one UI group.
blocker2ContactBundleNotAtomic.fix: Kept the existing 5 RPCs exactly as they are (no new DB-wide transaction, no SQL). Split the bundle internally into FOUR independent sub-writes, matching the mandate's own bullet-list grouping exactly: publicContact (phone+email), whatsapp (number+enabled-state as ONE sub-group, per the mandate's single-bullet listing of 'WhatsApp number / enabled state'), restaurantSettings (lang+address+hours), trackingText (statusTexts). Each sub-write has its own pure *SubDirty comparator (publicContactSubDirty, whatsappSubDirty, restaurantSettingsSubDirty, trackingTextSubDirty), its own attemptedCount++/try/catch, and its own partial generalSnapshotRef advance ONLY for the fields it itself persisted. On any sub-write's failure, the SAME shared stContactSaveError visual message is used (explicitly permitted by the mandate: 'you may keep one visual error message for the contact section'), but the internal dirty state stays field/subgroup-accurate: a failed sub-write's fields remain dirty and are retried in isolation; a succeeded sub-write's fields become clean and are never rewritten by a retry. The pre-existing three-way outcome mechanism (success / direct failure / stPartialSaveError-prefixed mixed) needed ZERO new code to correctly report contact-bundle partial failures -- succeededCount/failedKeys are simply populated at finer (per-sub-write) granularity automatically.
blocker2ContactBundleNotAtomic.k5ContinueDecision: The four sub-writes are attempted in their original, unchanged order (publicContact -> whatsapp -> restaurantSettings -> trackingText) and are NEVER aborted by an earlier sub-write's failure -- all four are still attempted independently every submit, to maximize what actually gets persisted and keep reporting granular. Explicitly chosen and tested (K5) over a 'stop at first failure' design.
blocker2ContactBundleNotAtomic.sharedVisualErrorMessageRetained: stContactSaveError, pushed by any of the four sub-writes' catch blocks -- never falsely called 'atomic'
